messages:
sam: Heads-up — noticed a host-side latency reg after last night's kernel-selector tweak. p50 looks fine but p95 and p99 for short (<16 token) streams jumped ~18-22%.
kevin: ugh. saw any correlation with batching changes or is this purely parse/stream overhead?
tasha: can you paste the flamegraph? maybe tokenization/runtime handoff got slower.
sam: paste from x-profiler: ```
# sample stack (host, short stream)
parse_request -> header_normalize -> minibuffer_slice -> token_shim -> writev_flush -> grpc_poll -> kernel_dispatch
CPU%: header_normalize 12%, token_shim 28%, writev_flush 20%
```
maya: token_shim 28% is WTF. that module was slimmed down. did we reintroduce allocations?
kevin: I ran a local with `--snapshot-ministream` and saw extra memcopy in header_normalize when the client uses HTTP2 but falls back to grpc path. looks like new header packing logic copies twice.
tasha: ah that matches: change #6423 replaced in-place slice with safe copy for edge cases. safe but costly.
sam: perf-bot traced request path counts — when seq_len<16 we hit `smallwrite-path` and it does `memcpy(>512)` twice.
perf-bot: trace summary: smallwrite-path invocations up 3.1x, avg memcpy per req 820 bytes, extra syscalls up 2.6x.
kevin: quick mitigation: revert kernel-selector flag that coerces grpc route for some http2 headers, it forces the grpc framing path even for plain text clients. that reduces the double-pack.
maya: can we instead change the header_normalize to detect already-packed frames and skip copy? cheaper than reverting kernel selector.
tasha: yep feasible. jumping into a patch: avoid copy if `frame_flags & FRAME_PACKED` is set. but need test for malformed headers.
sam: timeline — we should hotfix today. two options: 1) revert selector flag (low-risk rollback) 2) patch header_normalize (lower perf impact, medium risk).
kevin: rollback is fastest. do rollback -> observe metrics -> then patch and re-deploy.
maya: +1. I'll prepare rollback PR and a guarded patch PR.
kevin: also check KV cache churn — this regression increases tiny requests which amplify KV lookup rate. saw a KV miss rate bump on the affected hosts.
sam: KV miss bump was small but correlated. per-host kv-ops up 12% on tail windows. might push eviction thrash.
tasha: add a quick cache heatmap: `kv-monitor --window=5m --tags=host=canary` — wants to see shard hotness.
perf-bot: kv-monitor output (canary cluster): "hot_shards: 7 -> 11, avg_latency_ms: 1.9 -> 2.6"
maya: ok that suggests we should also throttle smallwrite-path or add coalescing for micro-requests until kernel/path normalized.
kevin: we can add a short prefix cache for stream-prefetch: if first chunk < X bytes, stash and wait 10ms for more fragments to combine. avoids writev syscall storms.
sam: potential side-effect: 10ms wait may hurt single-token latency. but this pain is primarily on p99 of heavy short streams.
tasha: can make it adaptive: only enable coalesce when host load high and batching heuristics predict high volume. config: `ministream_coalesce_ms=adaptive` with threshold on rps>2000.
maya: testing checklist: rollback PR -> measure p95/p99 in canary -> enable adaptive coalesce (off by default) -> apply header_normalize patch -> re-enable selector if still desired.
kevin: also add e2e perf test for short-stream hotpath. current CI misses grpc+http2 mixed clients. create a `shortstream-1000x` nightly.
sam: created an issue: https://redwood/issue/INF-1429 for the e2e test and canary plan.
tasha: smallish patch ready, I'll open PR and label `hotfix` after rollback lands.
maya: rollback PR up: `revert: selector coercion #6423` -> deploy to canary now?
sam: deploy-bot: canary deploy started for build `2026.03.20-rc3`.
deploy-bot: canary deploy finished — instances: canary-a,b,c.
sam: initial canary numbers: p95 down from +22% back to baseline, p99 still ~+5%.
kevin: good. merge patch soon. I'll instrument writev traces to ensure we don't reintroduce memcopy.
tasha: PR opened: `header_normalize: skip copy on FRAME_PACKED when safe` -> reference INF-1429.
maya: after header patch, let's run shortstream-1000x job.
sam: thanks all. follow-ups: (1) KV heatmap alert threshold (2) add shortstream nightly (3) measure coalesce impact on single-token tail.
kevin: leaving notes in the PR, tagging ops to watch KV. :eyes:
maya: thanks — will follow-up on metrics in #eng-sre once canary fully ramps. :thumbsup:
